english: 128 Chronography of Barhebraeus.

And after these things, al-Mahdi marched against the territory of the Romans,
and he encamped by the river Pyramos in the district of Arabissos.
And his son Harun captured the fortress of Semaluos, and took captives, and departed.
And in the year 1092
of the Greeks?], the Arabs took about seven thousand captives from Ephesus,
and four thousand also of the Arabs died.
King Leo, however, sent an army and exiled the Orthodox Syrian {OCR?} people,
and settled them in Thrace.
And it is said
that this King Leo also was a hater of icons and attached to the Orthodox, like his father.
And in that same year Leo died,
and Constantine, his son, reigned for twenty-two years.
Because he was small when he became king,
his mother Irene administered [the kingdom] and was proclaimed together with him.
In the year 1094
[1094], al-Mahdi sent his son Harun against the royal city [Constantinople].
And the Romans devised a stratagem,
and they hemmed in the Arabs by the river Sangarios,
such that on one side was the mountain,
and on the other side was the water.
And when the Arabs were hard pressed,
they sought peace for three years.
And Irene, according to the female mind, consented,
and the Arabs withdrew.
And after a year, Ali {OCR: al-Mahdi?} rebuilt the city of al-Hadath.
After al-Mahdi {OCR: 'hdi'}, Musa his son [reigned] one year and a month and a half.
Before this one began to reign,
that is, in the year 1095
[1095 {OCR: 1025}] of the Greeks (784 of our Lord?):
winged locusts came and ruined the crops,
and laid eggs {lit. cast seed}.
And it hatched out and crawled, climbing up walls and partitions,
and entered into houses through windows and doors.
And even the water-jars, beds, tables, and basins were filled with it.
And when it entered a house from the south side,
it would go out from the north side.
And together with grass and trees, it ate also woolen garments and the clothes of men.
And when it had consumed the whole district of Edessa and Sarug,
it passed to the west.
And for three years after this severe chastisement,
there was a famine in the land.
And in the year 1097
[1097], the Romans went out and destroyed al-Hadath, which had recently been built by the Arabs,
and they ruined it and completely demolished its walls.
And in that same year Musa died in the month of Tammuz.
After Musa, Harun al-Rashid his brother [reigned] twenty-three years and two months.
This one sent Abd al-Malik,
